runs.t: Every Farmings animal carries its own genome. It is stored on the animal and saved with the world, and it decides what the animal is good at and what it looks like.

items.t: have eight core traits: milk yield, butterfat, protein, feed efficiency, health, fertility, longevity and temperament.
have wool yield, fleece quality, feed efficiency, health, fertility, longevity, temperament and hardiness, plus milk yield for dairy sheep.
Each breed starts from baseline scores on a
scale. These are game-balance targets, not real breed averages.
A calf takes half its genes from each parent. Its breed mix is the average of its parents'.
The same parents and the same seed always give the same young.
Labels follow the mix: purebred, influenced, cross or composite.

runs.t: The look comes from real colour genes, kept beside the trait genes:

Sheep: white over coloured, black heads, horns, wool or hair coat. Coloured lambs turn up now and then.
Pigs, goats and horses have their own colour genes.
